paragraphs: Here's what I want you to take home, friend. Holiness doesn't rub off, but defiled does. The priests said so themselves: consecrated meat in a garment doesn't make the bread holy (Haggai 2:12), but touching a corpse makes whatever you touch defiled (Haggai 2:13). So Haggai says the LORD calls the people's work defiled too, and that tells us busy hands can't make a heart clean (Haggai 2:14).

Now look at what the LORD says about the hard times. He struck the work of their hands with blight, mildew and hail, "but you did not turn to Me" (Haggai 2:17). That's the heart of it. He wanted them back with Him more than He wanted their harvest. I think a lot of us read a rough season and ask what went wrong with the stuff, when the LORD is asking us to turn to Him.

And then comes the best part. The vine, the fig, the pomegranate and the olive tree had not yet yielded fruit, and still the LORD says, "But from this day on, I will bless you" (Haggai 2:19). He spoke that promise to His people in Haggai's day, on the day the foundation of His temple was laid (Haggai 2:18). I think that shows us a God who gives His word before the harvest shows up, so, baker, turning to Him is always the right move.
